excerpt: They started from 17 candidate features. These include things like the number of and types of instructions and memory level parallelism (MLP) within an OpenCL kernel. Table I gives the list of candidate features used in [15]. ... Principal Component Analysis ... is applied to map the 17 candidate features into 7 aggregated features, so that each aggregated feature is a linear combination of the original features.
overview: This passage provides a concrete instance of feature engineering in compiler learning: static LLVM-derived code features are chosen for OpenCL kernels and then compressed with PCA. It supports the claim that feature dimensionality is not a cosmetic concern; it affects the amount of data needed and the model’s ability to ignore redundant program descriptions.
title: OpenCL Feature Reduction
